note: Beaver County campground on Black Nugget Lake, a reclaimed coal mine, between Tofield and Ryley. Sites are spread around the lake: the main powered loop sits back from the south shore behind a meadow and trees, while sites on the west peninsula and along the north roads lie beside the water for shore fishing. Day-use areas and two boat launches; non-powered boating only. Seasonal campers hold sites 23-32. --Claude
summary: County page (Wayback Aug 2026; live page 403) + Let's Camp: 90 sites, C$30 non-serviced / C$36 power / C$42 full service, 2026 season May 14 - Sep 28, standing 2-night minimum (3 on long weekends) now in booking.min_stay, 30-amp, showers/dump/concession; lakeview kept with a lakefront lead for the peninsula sites.
flags: WATERFRONT (stored lakeview, checked hard): KEEP lakeview at least; LEAD (reviewer's call, no upgrade made): several sites sit at the water with open ground between. Esri imagery of the west peninsula shows RVs parked on the open sand pads ~10-25 m from the lake with nothing between; Let's Camp describes sites 45, 46, 50 ('Next to lake for shore fishing'), 61, 62, 64, 66, 67 ('next to lake'), T3 ('Right next to the water', tent) and group G2 ('right along the water'). The main powered loop (sites 1-31 area) is ~90 m back from the south shore behind a meadow and a tree band - not waterfront; east-road sites have the road between them and the water. A 'lakefront with a caveat naming the sites' value would follow the 'few clear waterfront sites count' rule, but the site numbers on the map are not labelled, so I could not tie each number to a pad.

MINIMUM STAY: standing 2-night minimum ('reservations require a minimum two-day stay, extending to three days on long weekends'; Let's Camp minNights 2) - recorded in booking.min_stay; a 2-night standing minimum is within the keep rule.
SEASONALS: new for 2026, powered sites 23-32 are seasonal (C$3,500); Let's Camp tags 10 of ~79 RV sites 'Seasonals'. Local campground, nightly majority - no concern.
